quotes: Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability. Complex systems tend to fail in mysterious ways, while straightforward designs fail gracefully.
Premature optimization is the root of all evil in programming. Measure bottlenecks empirically before refactoring for performance.
Concurrency is about dealing with lots of things at once. Parallelism is about doing lots of things at once.
The UNIX philosophy emphasizes building modular software tools that do one thing extraordinarily well and compose together seamlessly.
The best code is no code at all. Every line of code added to a codebase is a line that must be tested, debugged, and maintained forever.
